checks.claim: C1: actual model, class B and X, representatives, and scoped inputs
checks.reason: The note uses the real d1 Riesz kernel c_Gamma|x|^-alpha dx for 0<alpha<1 and the white kernel c_Gamma delta_0 at alpha=1, with amplitude kept. This agrees with H:homog at d=1, since scale homogeneity excludes |x|^-1 dx as a Radon measure. kappa=(4-alpha-a)/(3-alpha) and Q2 match consumer (24). B with the sum norm is complete because Cauchy sequences have L1 and L2 limits that agree locally in measure. B is separable because it embeds as a closed diagonal in L1xL2. Joint representatives exist: the simple-function subsequence converges in B for a.e. t and a.e. on boxes, using the global spacetime L1 bound. Null-set independence follows from Fubini and the norm estimates. The stochastic input is exactly the fixed-smooth-test bound (24) with finite Q2 and V_c^pos from (31)-(32), for the same canonical u. checks.reason: Integration gives int_0^1 K(s,t)dt=[s^(1-a)+(1-s)^(1-a)]/(1-a), with maximum 2^a/(1-a) at s=1/2 by concavity and symmetry. Cauchy-Schwarz and Fubini give (1). (1) applied to ||psi(t)||B gives absolutely convergent Bochner integrals for a.e. sigma and (2). Measurability follows from simple functions, whose coefficients are measurable in sigma. K>=1 on the unit square gives q_sigma>=q_avg, and q_avg is nonzero with positive finite mass. C_near=2c_Gamma/(1-alpha) and C_far=c_Gamma are correct, and (3) follows from Minkowski and the absolute integral. The far convolution tends to 0 by L1 approximation with bounded-support functions and kernel decay. White uses h=c_Gamma q in L2 with no far term. (4) follows from Cauchy-Schwarz, Hoelder and the split. (5) follows from applying Schur to the L2-L2 and L1-L1 components separately, then using ||f||1,||f||2<=||f||B. Tonelli gives exactly v=int int psi h. Positivity holds because K>=1 gives v>=int q_avg(Gamma*q_avg), which is positive in both the Riesz and white cases without continuity. (7) is bilinear polarization. Gamma, variance and Fourier conventions are unchanged.
